mode: offline, read-only; no live requests, no browser automation, no database mutation
percentile_method: statistics.quantiles(data, n=4, method='exclusive'), index 0 = p25, index 2 = p75
principle: Product Research comps value the verified slab identity, not the active listing that happened to represent it. Evidence is reused only where the full canonical slab_key is identical.
peer_eligibility_gates: USD proven on price, bid and shipping
acquisition_total present and complete - price alone is never substituted
data_note: no legacy listing row has shipping_state or acquisition_total persisted, so both were recomputed in memory from each stored raw payload with the current mapper. Nothing was written back.

surviving_provisional_opportunities.canonical_identity: 2023 PANINI PRIZM #343 ANTHONY RICHARDSON, base (parallel None), PSA NUMERIC 10, no qualifier, no autograph, no serial/print run
surviving_provisional_opportunities.fee_or_risk_buffer: none - the policy basis is explicitly gross, before taxes, import costs, marketplace fees and resale costs, so headroom before and after buffer are identical
unresolved_blockers: comps are stale: newest accepted sale 2025-05-15, 446 days old against a 365-day limit
active status is from the last crawl and was not re-verified, so the $30 listing may no longer exist or may no longer be at this price
two accepted comps ($160.00 and $48.33) are titled Lazer, a distinct Prizm parallel, against a base-card candidate
same seller lists an identical slab at $30 and $180, which is unexplained and may indicate a difference not captured by the parsed identity

parallel_leakage_finding.detail: 2 of 16 accepted comps are Lazer parallels matched to a base card. Removing them leaves n=14, median $63.25 unchanged, dispersion 8.65x -> 3.96x, headroom 43.1% unchanged.
parallel_leakage_finding.note: still above the 2.5x dispersion limit, so the WATCH downgrade holds either way. Reported because it is a comp-matching gap, not because it alters this result.

why_apparent_opportunities_disappear.summary: 92 of the 93 rescored candidates remain PASS. Re-pointing at the cheapest peer removes a large and systematic cost error but does not by itself create opportunities: the cards are mostly priced above market across every listing of the same slab.

smallest_deterministic_change: form exact verified slab groups on the full canonical slab_key first
within each group choose the member with the lowest complete acquisition_total among eligible members only
rank groups for research order by intra-slab dispersion, used only as a screening prior and never as evidence of market value
Product Research still makes the valuation decision
identity provenance selects the group, never the member
research one listing per exact slab identity unless its evidence is stale or otherwise unusable
selection_redesign.concrete_edit: export_pilot.build currently takes cand_id from peers.affected_groups, which keys on Tier B provenance. It would instead pick the cheapest eligible member of the same group. That is one function, and the eligibility gates above already exist in db.to_row and db.is_usd.

evidence_storage_recommendation.question: should Product Research evidence be keyed by slab identity rather than cand_id?
evidence_storage_recommendation.recommendation: resolve at read time, no schema change
evidence_storage_recommendation.why: sold_comps.candidate_item_id already joins to cards.item_id, which carries slab_key, so comps can be gathered by slab identity with a join today. Where Tier B re-keyed an identity, the join must use effective_slab_key rather than the raw parse. Adding a slab_key column to sold_comps would duplicate a derived value and would go stale the next time an identity is re-keyed.
evidence_storage_recommendation.guard: reuse only on exact full slab_key equality; never across partial, failed, legacy or differently qualified identities
